title: An in silico to in vivo approach identifies retinoid-X receptor activating tert-butylphenols used in food contact materials.
authors: Mengeling, Brenda J; Ettayapuram Ramaprasad, Azhagiya Singam; Smith, Martyn T; Turkieh, Dania; Kleinstreuer, Nicole C; Mansouri, Kamel; Durkin, Kathleen A; La Merrill, Michele A; Furlow, J David
one_liner_zh: 该文用机器学习筛选与RXR结合的食品接触化学物，结合分子建模分析配体-受体互作，虽非TF-DNA结合建模，但涉及核受体DNA结合伴侣及可迁移的AI筛选与结构建模方法，对TF-DNA互作研究有间接启发。
abstract: The potential for food contact chemicals to disrupt genetic programs in development and metabolism raises concerns. Nuclear receptors (NRs) control many of these programs, and the retinoid-X receptor (RXR) is a DNA-binding partner for one-third of the NRs. RXR disruption could generate adverse outcomes in several NR pathways. We used machine learning and other in silico methods to identify RXR-interacting candidates from a list of over 57,000 chemicals. Butylphenols comprised the largest, high-probability, structural group (58 compounds); several are food contact chemicals with widespread commercial use. In vitro ToxCast data suggested that bulky, aliphatic substitution at C4 of 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol facilitated RXR activation. We tested six butylphenols with increasing bulk at C4 in vivo for their ability to disrupt thyroid hormone receptor (TR) signaling, using an integrated luciferase reporter driven by TR-RXR binding and quantifiable morphological changes in a Xenopus laevis precocious metamorphosis assay. Three tert-butylphenols potentiated TH action at nanomolar concentrations. Molecular modeling showed the three positives formed more frequent, stable interactions with RXRalpha, and bulkiness at C4 increased steric complementarity with the RXR ligand-binding pocket. Our findings establish a paradigm for machine learning coupled with a convenient, in vivo validation approach to identify chemicals interacting with RXR-NR-controlled genetic pathways.
abstract_zh: 食品接触化学品干扰发育和代谢中遗传程序的可能性引发了关注。核受体（nuclear receptors, NRs）控制着许多此类程序，而维甲酸X受体（retinoid-X receptor, RXR）是三分之一的NRs的DNA结合伙伴。RXR的干扰可能在多个NR通路中产生不良后果。我们使用机器学习和其他计算机模拟方法，从超过57,000种化学品的列表中识别出与RXR相互作用的候选物质。丁基酚类构成了最大、高概率的结构组（58种化合物）；其中几种是广泛商业使用的食品接触化学品。体外ToxCast数据表明，2,6-二叔丁基酚C4位上的大体积脂肪族取代促进了RXR激活。我们测试了六种在C4位具有递增体积的丁基酚类，在体内评估其干扰甲状腺激素受体（thyroid hormone receptor, TR）信号传导的能力，使用由TR-RXR结合驱动的整合荧光素酶报告基因，以及在非洲爪蟾（Xenopus laevis）早熟变态试验中可量化的形态学变化。三种叔丁基酚在纳摩尔浓度下增强了TH作用。分子建模显示，这三种阳性化合物与RXRalpha形成了更频繁、稳定的相互作用，且C4位的体积增加了与RXR配体结合口袋的立体互补性。我们的发现建立了一种范式，将机器学习与便捷的体内验证方法相结合，以识别与RXR-NR控制的遗传通路相互作用的化学品。
